item.text:
### (a) Three social posts

1. We oppose commercial deep-sea mining because it will permanently destroy deep-ocean ecosystems. The ocean floor is a living world, not an industrial sacrifice zone. We must protect it before extraction begins.

2. We cannot replace deep-ocean ecosystems once mining destroys them. Commercial deep-sea mining will cause permanent damage—not a temporary disturbance. We demand protection, not permission to destroy.

3. We reject the claim that destroying the deep ocean is progress. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will permanently destroy deep-ocean ecosystems. We stand for an ocean protected from extraction.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We will not accept the permanent destruction of the deep ocean as the price of progress. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will permanently destroy deep-ocean ecosystems. These living worlds are not empty spaces waiting for industry; they are irreplaceable parts of our planet. We reject a future in which extraction takes priority over their survival. Our responsibility is clear: protect the deep ocean before mining begins, not promise to repair it after the damage is done. We are calling for a halt to commercial deep-sea mining, and we will keep organising, speaking out and demanding decisions that put ocean protection ahead of short-term profit.
